tagline: Down the North Platte on the line of the Oregon Trail.
intro: From the Wyoming line, US 26 and NE 92 come down the North Platte valley on the line of the Oregon, California and Mormon trails. From Scottsbluff to Lewellen the two highways and the river braid together for 91 miles, crossing and recrossing, past Chimney Rock and through Bridgeport, Lisco and Oshkosh. Below Lewellen, US 26 crosses the North Platte again, goes through Ash Hollow and comes down past Lake McConaughy to Ogallala.
The highway used to keep north of the river there. When Kingsley Dam made the lake in the 1930s, the road was moved to its present line.

moments.title: Mitchell Pass
moments.text: Emigrants called the gap between the bluffs Devil's Gap for its howling winds, and after 1851 the wagons, the Pony Express and the first transcontinental telegraph all went through it.

moments.title: Chimney Rock
moments.text: A landmark of all three trails, this spire of clay, volcanic ash and sandstone, has been worn shorter since the wagon days by erosion, lightning and, reportedly, cannon fire.

moments.title: Ash Hollow
moments.text: At Windlass Hill the wagons came down off the high table lands at a 25-degree pitch for about 300 feet, and their ruts still mark the slope.
